alpha-arasaka.name: ARASAKA CONTROL // ALPHA KIT
alpha-arasaka.overview: Arasaka Control is a defensive midrange deck that uses cheap blockers and removal to survive the early game, then deploys high-value threats to dominate the late game. The deck leverages Saburo Arasaka's passive ability to buff all red units, creating a resilient board state that's hard to break.

gameplan.early: Survive with cheap blockers (Corpo Security, Ruthless Lowlife). Sell excess lands and low-impact cards to build RAM. Avoid overcommitting to the board — you want to force your opponent to overextend.
gameplan.mid: Deploy your high-impact units (Swordwise Huscle, Goro Takemura). Use removal (Industrial Assembly) to clear threats. Start pressuring with Mantis Blades + Sandevistan combos.
gameplan.late: Once you have board control, Saburo Arasaka makes all your units massive. Close out with buffed attackers. Emergency Atlus provides life cushion if needed.

winConditions: Board control through efficient trades + removal

eddiesCurve.description: Arasaka wants to hit 4-5 Eddies by turn 3-4 to deploy key threats. Your curve is top-heavy, so you NEED to sell aggressively.
sellTargets: Low-impact units when you have better options

onThePlay: Keep 2-3 drop units to contest early board
Mulligan away expensive cards (Armored Minotaur, Saburo)
onTheDraw: Keep card draw (Corporate Surveillance if desperate)
You have an extra draw, so you can keep slightly greedier hands
neverKeep: Saburo Arasaka (too slow for opening hand)
Multiple copies of the same Legend

keySynergies.description: Equip Mantis Blades to a unit, then use Sandevistan to give it Quick (attack immediately). This enables surprise kills and racing damage.
Saburo's passive gives +1/+1 to all your red units. Every Corpo Security becomes a 2/3, every Swordwise Huscle becomes a 4/3. This snowballs hard.
Yorinobu's ability lets you sacrifice units for value. Pair with Industrial Assembly to clear threats while developing board.
Goro buffs units when they block. Corpo Security becomes a nightmare to attack into with Goro on board.

vs-merc-aggro.gameplan: Your entire deck is built to counter aggro. Mulligan for early blockers (Corpo Security, Ruthless Lowlife). Trade efficiently — you have more value in the late game. Emergency Atlus is your safety net.
tips: Don't race damage — you WILL lose. Block everything.
Save Industrial Assembly for their equipped units (Dying Night, Kiroshi Optics).
Once you stabilize, Saburo wins the game automatically.

suggestedUpgrades.reason: Better card draw engine than Corporate Surveillance
Premium removal + life gain, upgrades over Industrial Assembly
Late-game bomb that can steal opponent's units

commonMistakes: Selling Mantis Blades early — this is your best card, NEVER sell it
Overcommitting to the board vs aggro — you don't need to race, just survive
Keeping Saburo in opening hand — he's a late-game card, mulligan him away
Not using Yorinobu's sacrifice ability — free value is free value

alpha-merc.name: MERC AGGRO // ALPHA KIT
alpha-merc.overview: Merc Aggro is a fast, aggressive deck that aims to deal 20 damage before the opponent stabilizes. The deck uses cheap units, equipment, and combat tricks to push damage early and close out games before slower decks can react.

gameplan.early: Deploy cheap units (Secondhand Bombus, Evelyn Parker) and equip them with weapons (Dying Night, Kiroshi Optics). Attack every turn. Sell excess cards to keep the pressure on.
gameplan.mid: Use Floor It and Reboot Optics to push through blockers. T-Bug and Delamain Cab provide card advantage to refuel. Keep attacking — you can't afford to slow down.
gameplan.late: If the game goes long, you're in trouble. Use Jackie Welles (Legend) to finish with burst damage, or rely on MT0D12 Flathead to push the last points of damage.

winConditions: Early equipment snowball (Dying Night + cheap units)
Tempo advantage through combat tricks (Floor It, Reboot Optics)
Jackie Welles + Viktor Vektor combo for burst damage

eddiesCurve.description: Merc Aggro wants to hit 2-3 Eddies by turn 2-3 to deploy threats. You're a low-curve deck, so you can sell aggressively after turn 3-4.
sellTargets: Situational cards (Reboot Optics if they have no units)
High-cost cards if stuck in early game (MT0D12 Flathead)

onThePlay: Keep aggressive 1-2 drops (Secondhand Bombus, Evelyn Parker)
Keep 1 weapon (Dying Night or Kiroshi Optics)
Mulligan away card draw (T-Bug, Delamain Cab) — you need threats
onTheDraw: Can keep 1 card draw spell (T-Bug) if you have 2 units already
Still mulligan away late-game cards (MT0D12 Flathead)
neverKeep: MT0D12 Flathead (too slow for opening hand)
Multiple copies of the same weapon

keySynergies.description: Equip Dying Night to your 1-drop on turn 2. This creates a 3-power attacker that demands an answer immediately.
Kiroshi Optics gives +2 power AND draws a card when equipped. This is insane value — always prioritize playing this.
Jackie deals damage when he attacks. Viktor heals damage. Together, they create a racing engine that's hard to stop.
Floor It gives +3 power for a turn. Combo this with an already-equipped unit to push lethal damage or win combat.
Both cards draw you extra cards. Use them to refuel after your initial hand runs out.

vs-arasaka-control.gameplan: You MUST win before turn 6-7. Mulligan for your fastest hands (1-drop + weapon). Attack every turn. Use Floor It to push through their blockers. If they stabilize with Emergency Atlus, you lose.
tips: Don't hold back — you can't afford to play around removal
Save Floor It for lethal or winning a key combat
If they have Corpo Security, use Reboot Optics to tap it before attacking
Count their life total — you need to deal 20 damage FAST

suggestedUpgrades.reason: Better weapon than Dying Night, gives trample damage
Alternative Legend that gives your units haste

commonMistakes: Holding back damage — you're aggro, ATTACK EVERY TURN
Selling Dying Night or Kiroshi Optics — these are your best cards
Playing around removal — you don't have time, just go for it
Not using Viktor Vektor's ability — free life is free life
